title: Benko Gambit: the ideas
line: Black gives a pawn to open two files on the queen's side for its rooks.

steps.text: White starts by pushing the pawn in front of its queen two squares, into the center.
Bring the knight out. For now it stops White's other center pawn from coming to e4.
Push the pawn on c7 two squares. It attacks White's pawn on d4 from the side.
Offer a pawn: push the pawn on b7 two squares.

also.e7e6: That is the Benoni Defense, also sound. This lesson goes on with the gambit.

steps.after: This is the Benko Gambit. White takes the pawn.

steps.text: Offer another one. Black wants the files on the queen's side open.
Take back with the bishop. The file in front of your rook is open.
steps.after: Black stays a pawn down, often into the endgame. The open files have to make up for it.

steps.text: Move the pawn in front of your queen one square, to make room for your other knight.
Trade bishops. White's king has to take back, so it can no longer castle.
Push the pawn on g7 one square, to make room for your other bishop.
steps.after: Black is a pawn down, but its bishop will go to the long diagonal and its rooks to the open files, all aimed at White's queen's side.

summary: Black gives a pawn to open two files for its rooks, and trades bishops so White's king cannot castle.
